item.title: Version 2.8 (18)
item.description:
What's New in Version 2.8

  • Folders that share a name export in full When two folders had the same name — a subfolder named like a top-level folder, or "Notes" in both iCloud and On My Mac — only one of them was exported. Now both are, together, as the list shows them, and Auto Export no longer stops with "Some notes could not be read" because of it.
  • PDFs that look like Apple Notes Lines are no longer cut in half or repeated where a page ends. A title set in Notes' Title style is that size in the PDF, spacing matches Apple's own export, checklists show Notes' ticked circles, and links, tags and mentions keep their colour.
  • Every photo shows as a photo Pictures saved as AVIF or WebP, common for images saved from the web, appeared as file icons instead of the picture. They now appear in every format, and Word documents convert HEIC, WebP and AVIF so Word can show them.
  • PDFs inside notes show their pages A PDF shown inline in a note came out as a broken image. Its pages now appear in the export.
  • Tags and mentions stay where you typed them #tags and @mentions no longer break onto lines of their own, and a heading that contains a link is no longer split in two.
  • Cleaner Markdown and plain text Plain text no longer contains stray HTML tags or codes like &, tables come out as tables instead of run-together words, checklists keep their ticks and numbered lists keep their numbers.
  • Word documents that always open A note containing an invisible control character could produce a Word file that would not open. It no longer does.
  • Folders open smoothly Opening a large folder no longer shows an empty list or closes the folder again. Its notes appear as they load, and ticking them responds instantly.
  • Exports say what they could not show If an attachment was saved but could not be drawn in the finished file, the export now names it instead of reporting success.
  • Important updates come first When a future update fixes something that affects your exports, exporting and scheduled backups pause until it is installed, with an Install Update button right there. Your notes stay safe in Apple Notes in the meantime.

Updating from 2.6? Version 2.7 also brought a rebuilt Auto Export with a dashboard, backups that mirror your notes, Obsidian, Evernote, CSV, XML and OPML exports, links between notes that keep working, and backups to your own S3-compatible storage.

item.title: Version 2.7 (17)
item.description:
What's New in Version 2.7

  • Auto Export, rebuilt Setting up a schedule is now four short steps, and once it is running you get a dashboard: when the next exports are due, what each run did, and every setting in one place. Run one early with Export Now.
  • Backups that match your notes A backup now mirrors Apple Notes by default — only what changed is rewritten, and a note you delete leaves the backup. Prefer a dated copy of every run? Keep every backup instead.
  • Five new formats Obsidian, Evernote (ENEX), CSV, XML and OPML. The Obsidian vault arrives with front matter and working [[wikilinks]]; CSV is one spreadsheet with a row per note. EPUB now produces a proper book, one chapter per note.
  • Links between notes keep working A link to another note now opens that note's exported file, or its section in a combined document. Web links survive in Markdown and Text exports, which previously kept the words and lost the address.
  • Recently Deleted stays out Deleted notes are no longer exported as an ordinary folder. Switch on "Include Recently Deleted" if you want them.
  • Handwritten notes export their artwork Apple Pencil drawings and scanned pages now export as the drawing itself rather than a placeholder, and folders show how many handwritten notes they hold.
  • Tables keep their shape Columns come out in the order they were written, in every format that has tables.
  • Large libraries export without filling the disk A library of big PDF attachments could push a PDF export past 15 GB. It no longer does.
  • One document, when you want one Any export can be written as a single file with a table of contents instead of a file per note.
  • Exports that tell you the truth A run that could not save something names the note it belonged to, and no longer reports problems it did not have.
  • Back up to storage you own Send a copy of every export to your own S3-compatible bucket — AWS, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi or MinIO. Your bucket, your credentials, your bill; nothing goes to our servers. Off until you set it up, with a Test Connection button that checks it before you rely on it.
  • Notifications Scheduled exports run with nobody watching, so the app now asks to notify you, and says plainly when notifications are switched off.

item.title: Version 2.6 (13)
item.description:
What's New in Version 2.6

  • Attachments stay linked to their notes HTML and Markdown exports now include a working link to every attachment, with its real name. Links with spaces, & or # in the filename open correctly.
  • Fixed a crash when exporting from the database Exporting a larger library could quit the app unexpectedly.
  • No more missing attachments The AppleScript method kept only some attachments and silently skipped the rest. It now saves every type.
  • Notes that previously wouldn't open Some older notes exported as "Unable to extract note content". They now export normally.
  • Password-protected notes are shown Locked notes are marked in the list and in the folder they belong to, and explain themselves in exports instead of appearing empty.
  • PDF exports match Apple Notes Same page size, margins and text size — plus no blank final page, and the title no longer appears twice.
  • Markdown keeps its formatting Monospaced blocks stay monospaced, and images keep their original names.
  • Honest export summaries An export that could not save something now says so, rather than reporting success.
  • Auto export reliability Failures are reported instead of announced as successes, scheduled runs no longer repeat, and an export that finds nothing is treated as a problem rather than a completed backup.
  • Your licence survives a reset Resetting app data no longer signs you out, and you can now release a licence yourself before moving to a new Mac.

item.title: Version 2.3 (9)
item.description:
What's New in Version 2.3 (9)

  • Refreshed design A cleaner activation screen and a tidier, easier-to-use home page.
  • Smarter folder selection Choosing a folder now includes all of its notes right away.
  • Better exports Fixed code blocks in Markdown and heading/formatting issues in text exports.
  • Polish & fixes throughout the app.

item.title: Version 2.0 (5)
item.description:
What's New in Version 2.0

  • Improved PDF exports Tables, checklists, and text spacing now mirror Apple Notes formatting even when using the direct database export path.
  • Auto export reliability Scheduled exports use an isolated exporter instance to prevent conflicts, improving background stability.
  • General fixes Better attachment handling and polish throughout the export pipeline.
